articles.title: Double Stars In Cepheus
articles.summary: An amateur astronomer recounts an evening observation session in Palo Alto, attempting to view double stars in the constellation Cepheus using a 6-inch Maksutov-Cassegrain telescope. Following a list from a "Sky & Telescope" article, the observer managed to resolve several wide pairs, including Delta, Beta, and Xi Cephei, despite initial challenges with atmospheric conditions and telescope thermal settling.

articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: The SJAA Activities Calendar details various events for November and December, including general meetings with guest speakers on topics like 'Oxymoronic Astronomy' and Jupiter's Europa, as well as multiple star parties at Houge Park and Fremont Peak. It also provides contact information for news and information, along with a note about insurance coverage for members at sponsored events.

articles.title: SJAA At Yosemite
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) held a successful observing event at Yosemite on September 11-12, 1998. Despite initial weather threats, the sky cleared, offering excellent seeing conditions and breathtaking views of objects like Jupiter, Saturn, and the Milky Way. A small crowd allowed for personalized instruction, and participants enjoyed the improved paved observing area with available electricity.

articles.title: Look Closely:
articles.summary: The article suggests an effective observing trick for astronomers: focusing on multiple celestial objects that are close to one another in a single session. This strategy minimizes the need to reposition the telescope and simplifies the process of star-hopping.

articles.title: On Aperture And Cassiopeia Clusters:
articles.summary: The author recounts observations of Cassiopeia clusters made on September 5-6, 1980, using a six-inch hand-held Newtonian telescope at 36x. They also mention a prior observation of NGC 225 from nearly twenty years earlier with 7x50 binoculars, and briefly note the use of a 55mm Vixen fluorite refractor.

articles.title: On The Peak:
articles.summary: The author frequently visits Fremont Peak alone, humorously describing the thrill of solitude amid imagined dangers like vampires and velociraptors. While sweeping their flashlight, they often spot animal eyes in the dark, but always maintain a lighthearted tone, despite a humorous, ominous note about previous solo visitors who have not been heard from since.

articles.title: On Refractorhilia:
articles.summary: This very short, humorous piece features the author jokingly denying an addiction to refractors, using the common phrase, 'I can quit any time I want.' It's a lighthearted take on the enthusiast's dilemma.

articles.title: On The New 70mm Vixen Refractor:
articles.summary: The article describes the new 70mm Vixen Refractor, highlighting its striking aesthetic design, featuring a gloss white tube and pale matte green fittings, which the author finds particularly elegant and finely drawn. Despite a personal penchant for custom paint jobs, the author is so impressed by the telescope's original appearance that they are having second thoughts about refinishing it, a sentiment noted by the editor as quite remarkable.

articles.title: Editor's Extras
articles.summary: This 'Editor's Extras' column previews Norm Sperling's upcoming humorous talk on the historical definition of 'planet' and announces that a new editor for the 'Ephemeris' has been secured, with the formal reveal to come from the new editor. It also highlights successful late summer club events and school star parties despite weather challenges, and calls for nominations for upcoming club elections.

articles.title: Akkana Peck
articles.summary: This article provides an astronomical observing guide for early November, detailing the visibility and key features of various planets and celestial objects. It highlights Mercury's greatest elongation, Mars's increasing size, Jupiter's equatorial activity including a double shadow transit, and the optimal viewing of Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and 1 Ceres. The guide offers specific viewing tips and resources like finder charts and an applet for predicting transit times.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: This article provides an astronomical forecast for November 1998, focusing on improved lunar viewing conditions as the Moon ascends towards its closest, largest, and brightest full phase of the year. It highlights specific celestial events, including close approaches by Aldebaran, Regulus, and Jupiter, and a daytime occultation of Mars on Friday the 13th. The author also discusses a strong northern libration offering unique views of lunar craters and offers general tips for optimal observation.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: This article provides an outlook for November meteor showers, focusing primarily on the Leonids, which are expected to produce high activity, potentially a storm, around November 16/17, 1998, due to the parent comet Tempel-Tuttle's upcoming perihelion. It highlights ideal observing conditions for the Leonids in 1998, particularly for the U.S. West Coast and China, and offers brief notes on the less favorable viewing prospects for the South and North Taurids.

articles.title: Bill Arnett
articles.summary: This article details the October 3rd board meeting, discussing various organizational matters including election procedures, the formation of a nominating committee, and the desire for incumbents and challengers to run. Key topics also included the unresolved issue of trees at Houge Park, the success of a magazine giveaway, and the expansion of the loaner program. Additionally, the need for a new astronomy class teacher and the sale of RASC handbooks and the SJAA APOD were addressed.

articles.title: From Page One
articles.summary: The author recounts their experience observing challenging double stars in Cepheus from their suburban backyard, utilizing an Intes telescope with a driven equatorial mount. Despite initial setup concerns, the drive proved invaluable for resolving close pairs at high magnifications (up to 375x), even under hazy conditions. The successful separation of objects like Struve 2764 and 2872 highlights the telescope's performance and the satisfaction of expanding observational limits through amateur astronomy.

articles.title: Yosemite
articles.summary: The article details the SJAA's rewarding summer visits to Glacier Point in Yosemite, where members enjoyed excellent skies for observing. An unseasonable rain prior to one trip offered the added bonus of restarted Yosemite Falls, though the best time for stargazing versus viewing the falls is discussed.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: The article describes an astronomy class led by Kevin Medlock on Double 10 Day, where he taught the basics of CCD imaging to beginners. Medlock's presentation involved both theoretical explanation and a practical outdoor demonstration of setting up equipment and capturing stunning images of celestial objects like the Ring Nebula and Andromeda Galaxy with short exposures. The event, despite minor technical hitches, was highly effective and left participants enthusiastic about the fun of CCD astrophotography.

articles.title: Jim Van Nuland
articles.summary: This article explores the early history of astronomy events and star parties at Fremont Peak, primarily focusing on the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). While SJAA officially started regular use of Fremont Peak after October 1975, records indicate an SJAA overnight star party there in August 1970, with further evidence suggesting continuous SJAA member star parties at the peak since mid-1966. Before late 1975, Fremont Peak events were often listed as "AANC star parties" in conjunction with groups like the San Francisco Sidewalk Astronomers.

articles.title: Astronomy Tutoring
articles.summary: SJAA members Mark Wagner and Rich Neuschaefer are offering tutoring sessions focused on Deep Sky and Lunar/Planetary observing. These sessions provide hands-on experience and expert guidance for amateur astronomers. Interested individuals can find more information on their website or contact the instructors directly.

articles.title: Directions to SJAA places
articles.summary: The article provides detailed driving directions to several key astronomical observing locations primarily used by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) and related groups. It offers specific routes from major highways to Houge Park, Henry Coe State Park, Fremont Peak State Park, and Grant Ranch County Park, noting important details like fees and specific club-designated areas. This guide aims to assist members and visitors in reaching star party sites efficiently.

articles.title: Activities Through Other Clubs
articles.summary: This article outlines various astronomical activities available through different clubs, encouraging SJAA members to participate. TAC offers Wednesday access to the Montebello site, PAS hosts public viewing at Foothill Observatory on clear Friday evenings and Saturday mornings, and HVAC organizes dark sky parties at Grant Ranch. Additionally, Chabot and San Francisco clubs are increasing their event offerings, expanding choices for Bay Area astronomers.

articles.title: November
articles.summary: The article announces two November meetings for the PAS: a general meeting on November 13th featuring Dr. James Lissauer of NASA Ames discussing "Planetary Ring Systems" at Foothill College, and a board meeting on November 18th at the Foothill College Observatory. Both events are scheduled for 7:30 pm.

articles.title: December
articles.summary: The document outlines the December schedule, featuring two key events for PAS. These include the Annual Meeting and Board Elections on December 11th, and a Board Meeting on December 16th, both taking place at Foothill College, with the latter at the college's observatory.

articles.title: John Gleason Needs No Introduction, And It's A Good Thing
articles.summary: John Gleason delivered an exceptional astrophotography class, acclaimed as one of the best presentations by the author despite initial logistical issues. The talk covered various techniques, historical context, and notably demonstrated the evolution of imaging with striking before-and-after photos, even showcasing high-quality inkjet prints of digitally enhanced images. The author praised Gleason's resilience and the class's educational value, expressing a strong desire for its continuation next year.

articles.title: Image Brightness
articles.summary: This article, 'Image Brightness,' discusses how to achieve maximum image brightness when using a telescope by ensuring the beam of light exiting the eyepiece fits within the observer's eye pupil. It explains that the exit pupil diameter is determined by the telescope's clear aperture divided by magnification, and provides formulas for calculating minimum magnification based on typical pupil sizes. The author also suggests slightly higher minimum magnifications for better viewing of faint deep-sky objects like galaxies.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: This article provides updates on several telescopic comets, noting Periodic Comet Howell's recent outburst and Giacobini-Zinner's current brightness. It details the discovery of Comet LONEOS-Tucker, found by Roy Tucker, and its estimated 8-year orbital period. Additionally, the piece offers insights into amateur comet hunting, analyzing the typical elongation (angle from the sun) at which visual comet discoveries are made and explaining why searches are concentrated near the sun.

articles.title: Ephemerides -- Epoch 2000, 0h UTC
articles.summary: This article presents detailed ephemerides for five comets (C/1997 J2, 21P/Giacobini-Zinner, C/1998 P1, 88P/Howell, and C/1998 M5) for Epoch 2000, 0h UTC. It provides tables with daily Right Ascension, Declination, elongation from the Sun, sky visibility, and estimated visual magnitude for observation between early November and early December, serving as a guide for observers.

articles.title: Orbital Elements -- Epoch 2000.0
articles.summary: This document presents a table of orbital elements for five celestial objects: Giacobini-Zinner, Meunier Dupouy, Williams, LINEAR, and Howell, all referenced to Epoch 2000.0. The data includes perihelion distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, orbital period, and absolute magnitude for each object. This information appears to be a section of an SJAA Ephemeris for November 1998.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document provides a directory of the organization's current officers and board of directors. It lists the names and contact phone numbers for the President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, and several Directors, outlining the leadership structure.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: This document lists the staff and program chairmen for an organization, including their names, roles, and contact information. It details key personnel for various programs such as the Mentoring Program, Observational Astronomy, School Star Parties, and the Telescope Loaner Program. Contact details for the editor, circulation, printing, and web page management are also provided.

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: Members of the SJAA are encouraged to submit articles for publication in the organization's Ephemeris newsletter. Submissions should be emailed to Dave North at Timocharis@aol.com.

articles.title: Finding Fremont Peak
articles.summary: This article provides detailed driving directions to Fremont Peak State Park, located south of San Juan Bautista. It outlines the route from Hwy 101 near Gilroy, guiding visitors via Hwy 156 and Hwy G-1, and notes a specific road jog and a $3 entrance fee.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program Status
articles.summary: The Telescope Loaner Program is currently active and available to all San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) members. Members interested in utilizing the program should contact Mike Koop directly at (408) 473-6315.

articles.title: Current Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes currently on loan, detailing the scope description, borrower, and due date. It also informs interested individuals that they can be placed on a waiting list for a scope once it becomes available after its due date. The list includes various types of telescopes such as Quantum S/C, Celestron S/C, Dobsonians, Solar Scopes, and Newt/P Mounts, with due dates spanning from October 1998 to January 1999.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document outlines an "Extended Scope Loans" program, detailing telescopes with prolonged borrowing periods. Individuals interested in these scopes can request to borrow them, and the organization will coordinate a transfer with the current borrower. A table provides details on specific telescopes currently on extended loan, including their borrowers and due dates.

articles.title: Available Scopes
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers various telescopes for immediate loan to its members. These scopes are currently stored at the homes of other SJAA members. Interested individuals can contact Mike Koop for pickup arrangements at any listed SJAA event.

articles.title: Waiting List
articles.summary: The document lists one item on a 'Waiting List': a 6-inch Newtonian telescope with a P Mount for Al Case. It also includes a note asking if anyone has space to store one or two scopes and provides contact information for Mike Koop.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: This document, titled 'Periodical Publication Statement', clarifies that the SJAA Ephemeris, the official newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, is published monthly. It is released 12 times a year, covering the period from January through December. The statement also includes the association's address.

articles.title: To Subscribe to/Unsubscribe from the SJAA Mailing List send email to:
articles.summary: This document outlines the procedure for subscribing to or unsubscribing from the SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association) mailing list. Users must send an email to sjaa-requests@seds.org with a blank subject line and a single text line in the body stating either "subscribe" or "unsubscribe."

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing membership fees ($15 for regular, $6 for junior) and an optional add-on subscription to Sky & Telescope magazine ($27). It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment either in person at an SJAA meeting or by mail to the treasurer. The form also includes contact information for the association.
